reproduction.mutation: In lot control-post-finish, add an external ingredient input of 70 kg and a terminal compost residue output of 70 kg; append both flow/load IDs to the lot, then bind terminal sources with _as_schema2.
reproduction.balance: The lot now has 140 kg input and 140 kg output: its original 70 kg long-path input plus 70 kg late ingredient, and 70 kg consumed product plus 70 kg compost residue.
reproduction.counterinterpretation: The declarations are also compatible with all 70 kg from the long path going to compost and all 70 kg of late ingredient going to human consumption. The lot-level witness cannot distinguish these allocations.

candidate_not_implemented.proposal: Opt-in per-lot rows assigning positive declared mass from each input flow to each output flow, with local references, unique pairs and input/output marginal sums checked against measured mass uncertainty. A flow-level witness would traverse only positive allocations and report flow IDs as well as lot IDs.
candidate_not_implemented.required_negative_control: Long-path input allocated entirely to compost and late ingredient entirely to consumed product must have no complete consumption witness.
candidate_not_implemented.required_positive_control: A valid mixed lot with a declared positive long-path contribution to the consumed output may have a witness, while schemas 1 and 2 retain their existing contracts.
candidate_not_implemented.limit: Even a complete allocation table would remain a declaration; a small positive allocation or a forged table does not establish physical composition, field impact, V or G.

limits: This is an invented fixture and an adversarial interpretation, not a measured food chain.
Schema 2 promises operational paths, not within-lot material attribution; valid:true is consistent with its documented limited contract.
No schema-3 code or field observation was introduced by this report.
